purpose: Define how OpenVA moves from bootstrap seed identity discovery to queue-driven, evidence-scored catalog growth without treating discovered vendors or sources as canonical truth.

stage_model.purpose: Use reviewed seed files to provide initial vendor identities and official domains for priority coverage areas.
stage_model.entry_condition: Coverage area has insufficient reviewed vendor identities.
stage_model.exit_condition: Seed files validate and produce enough reviewed vendor candidates for bounded source discovery.

stage_model.purpose: Use taxonomy coverage gaps, source-health debt, and candidate backlog state to decide which cohorts should be discovered next.
stage_model.entry_condition: Bootstrap seeds are no longer the primary candidate source for a coverage area.
stage_model.exit_condition: Candidate backlog has deduplicated, source-discovered, review-ready candidates.

stage_model.purpose: Promote only candidates with clear official-domain authority, core public-source evidence, and reviewed promotion plans.
stage_model.entry_condition: Candidate has source-discovery evidence and no blocking duplication or authority issues.
stage_model.exit_condition: Reviewed promotion plan is committed under maintenance/reviewed/ and applied by candidate-promotion-pr.yml.

stage_model.purpose: Use source-health and observation outputs to keep the expanded catalog fresh after promotion.
stage_model.entry_condition: Candidate has become a canonical catalog record.
stage_model.exit_condition: Source debt is repaired or truth-stated through the source maintenance loop.

promotion_readiness_dimensions.description: Candidate is likely to process personal data, support cross-border transfer, act as a subprocessor, or otherwise appear in vendor assurance workflows.
Candidate has a clear official domain and source URLs can be evaluated against that authority.
Candidate has at least one public source candidate from the core source type set and should trend toward DPA, subprocessors, privacy, and security coverage.
Candidate fills a priority taxonomy coverage area, regional gap, or underrepresented regulated-industry segment.
Candidate does not duplicate an existing canonical vendor, product surface, entity family, or reviewed candidate.
Catalog growth promotion should slow down when source debt exceeds the configured source-health budget.

batching_policy.rationale: Keep candidate-promotion PRs reviewable as the catalog grows beyond the bootstrap corpus.

guardrails: Do not scrape broad company registries as a substitute for coverage-area strategy.
Do not turn seed files into canonical vendor records.
Do not promote discovered candidates automatically.
Do not write data/vendors/** outside candidate-promotion-pr.yml.
Do not expand source types beyond the core set until discovery and promotion quality are proven.
Do not let catalog growth bypass source-health constraints.
